Listing Diagnostics

Deep dive into project-level diagnostic analysis with RoselineMCP.

Overview

The listDiagnostics tool provides detailed diagnostic information for specific projects, including statistics, fixability analysis, and filtering capabilities.

Basic Usage

List All Diagnostics for a Project

{
  "tool": "listDiagnostics",
  "parameters": {
    "project": "MyApp.Core"
  }
}

Specify Project by Path

{
  "tool": "listDiagnostics",
  "parameters": {
    "project": "/path/to/MyApp.Core/MyApp.Core.csproj"
  }
}

Filtering Options

Filter by Diagnostic IDs

Focus on specific diagnostic types:

{
  "tool": "listDiagnostics",
  "parameters": {
    "project": "MyApp.Core",
    "ids": ["CS0168", "CS0219", "IDE0005"]
  }
}

Filter by File Patterns

Analyze specific parts of your codebase:

{
  "tool": "listDiagnostics",
  "parameters": {
    "project": "MyApp.API",
    "files": ["**/Controllers/**", "**/Services/**"]
  }
}

Combine Filters

Use multiple filters together:

{
  "tool": "listDiagnostics",
  "parameters": {
    "project": "MyApp.Core",
    "ids": ["SA1101", "SA1200"],
    "files": ["**/Models/**"],
    "max": 50
  }
}

Understanding the Response

Complete Response Structure

{
  "project": "MyApp.Core",
  "totalDiagnostics": 234,
  "diagnostics": [
    {
      "project": "MyApp.Core",
      "file": "Services/UserService.cs",
      "line": 45,
      "column": 8,
      "id": "RCS1213",
      "severity": "warning",
      "message": "Remove unused member declaration"
    }
  ],
  "stats": {
    "byId": {
      "RCS1213": 12,
      "CS0168": 5,
      "SA1101": 23,
      "IDE0005": 8
    },
    "bySeverity": {
      "Error": 3,
      "Warning": 178,
      "Info": 53
    }
  },
  "suggestedFixableIds": [
    "CS0168",
    "IDE0005",
    "RCS1213",
    "SA1101"
  ]
}

Key Components

  1. totalDiagnostics: Total count before limiting
  2. diagnostics: Detailed list (limited by max parameter)
  3. stats: Statistical breakdown
  4. suggestedFixableIds: IDs that can be automatically fixed

Advanced Scenarios

Finding Unused Code

{
  "tool": "listDiagnostics",
  "parameters": {
    "project": "MyApp.Core",
    "ids": [
      "CS0168",  // Unused variable
      "CS0219",  // Variable assigned but never used
      "IDE0051", // Unused private member
      "IDE0052", // Unread private member
      "RCS1213"  // Unused member declaration
    ]
  }
}

Style Violations

{
  "tool": "listDiagnostics",
  "parameters": {
    "project": "MyApp.Core",
    "ids": [
      "SA1000",  // Spacing around keywords
      "SA1101",  // Prefix with 'this'
      "SA1200",  // Using directives placement
      "SA1600"   // Elements should be documented
    ]
  }
}

Performance Issues

{
  "tool": "listDiagnostics",
  "parameters": {
    "project": "MyApp.Core",
    "ids": [
      "CA1806",  // Do not ignore method results
      "CA1810",  // Initialize static fields inline
      "CA1822",  // Mark members as static
      "CA1827"   // Do not use Count when Any can be used
    ]
  }
}

Workflow Examples

1. Incremental Code Cleanup

# Step 1: Get overview
listDiagnostics --project MyApp.Core

# Step 2: Identify most common issues
# Look at stats.byId to find frequent problems

# Step 3: Focus on fixable issues
listDiagnostics --project MyApp.Core \
  --ids $(suggestedFixableIds)

# Step 4: Target specific files
listDiagnostics --project MyApp.Core \
  --files "**/Services/**" \
  --ids CS0168,IDE0005

2. Pre-commit Check

#!/bin/bash
# Check for critical issues before commit

RESULT=$(listDiagnostics --project MyApp.Core)
ERROR_COUNT=$(echo "$RESULT" | jq '.stats.bySeverity.Error // 0')

if [ "$ERROR_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "❌ Found $ERROR_COUNT errors. Please fix before committing."
    exit 1
fi

echo "✅ No errors found. Safe to commit."

3. Technical Debt Tracking

# track_debt.py
import json
import subprocess
from datetime import datetime

def track_project_debt(project_name):
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["listDiagnostics", "--project", project_name],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True
    )
    
    data = json.loads(result.stdout)
    
    metrics = {
        "date": datetime.now().isoformat(),
        "project": project_name,
        "total": data["totalDiagnostics"],
        "by_severity": data["stats"]["bySeverity"],
        "fixable_count": len(data["suggestedFixableIds"])
    }
    
    # Save to tracking file
    with open(f"{project_name}_metrics.json", "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(metrics) + "\n")
    
    return metrics

Analyzing Statistics

Interpreting byId Stats

The stats.byId section shows which diagnostics are most common:

"byId": {
  "SA1101": 45,  // Most common - focus on this first
  "IDE0005": 23,
  "CS0168": 12,
  "RCS1213": 8
}

Strategy: Fix the most common issues first for maximum impact.

Understanding Severity Distribution

"bySeverity": {
  "Error": 0,     // Good - no compilation errors
  "Warning": 45,  // Focus area
  "Info": 120,    // Suggestions for improvement
  "Hidden": 5     // Usually safe to ignore
}

Fixability Analysis

The suggestedFixableIds list shows which issues can be automatically resolved:

"suggestedFixableIds": [
  "CS0168",   // ✅ Can be auto-fixed
  "IDE0005",  // ✅ Can be auto-fixed
  "SA1101"    // ✅ Can be auto-fixed
  // CS1591 not listed - requires manual documentation
]

Integration Patterns

With CI/CD

# GitHub Actions example
- name: Check Code Quality
  run: |
    DIAGNOSTICS=$(listDiagnostics --project ${{ matrix.project }})
    
    # Extract metrics
    TOTAL=$(echo "$DIAGNOSTICS" | jq '.totalDiagnostics')
    ERRORS=$(echo "$DIAGNOSTICS" | jq '.stats.bySeverity.Error // 0')
    
    # Set output
    echo "total-diagnostics=$TOTAL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    echo "error-count=$ERRORS" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    
    # Fail if errors
    if [ "$ERRORS" -gt 0 ]; then
      exit 1
    fi

With Code Review

# Generate report for PR review
listDiagnostics --project MyApp.Core \
  --files $(git diff --name-only origin/main) \
  > pr-diagnostics.json

# Create markdown summary
echo "## Diagnostic Report" > report.md
echo "Total issues: $(jq '.totalDiagnostics' pr-diagnostics.json)" >> report.md
echo "### By Severity" >> report.md
jq -r '.stats.bySeverity | to_entries[] | "- \(.key): \(.value)"' pr-diagnostics.json >> report.md

Performance Considerations

Large Projects

For projects with many files:

  1. Use file filters to analyze subsets
  2. Limit results with max parameter
  3. Filter by IDs to focus on specific issues
  4. Process in batches for very large codebases

Memory Usage

  • Diagnostics are collected in memory
  • Large projects may require more memory
  • Consider splitting analysis by directory

Troubleshooting

Project Not Found

# Verify project exists
ls -la *.csproj

# Use full path
listDiagnostics --project /full/path/to/Project.csproj

No Diagnostics Returned

# Check if project builds
dotnet build MyApp.Core.csproj

# Verify analyzers are installed
dotnet list package | grep Analyzer

Timeout Issues

{
  "project": "LargeProject",
  "max": 100,  // Limit initial results
  "files": ["**/Priority/**"]  // Focus on priority files
}

Best Practices

  1. Regular Analysis: Run weekly to track trends
  2. Focus on Fixable: Prioritize suggestedFixableIds
  3. Track Metrics: Monitor diagnostic counts over time
  4. Incremental Improvement: Fix issues in small batches
  5. Combine with ApplyFixes: Use results to guide fixes

Quick Reference

Common Filter Combinations

Goal Parameters
Unused code ids: ["CS0168", "CS0219", "IDE0051", "RCS1213"]
Style issues ids: ["SA*"] (all StyleCop)
Performance ids: ["CA1806", "CA1822", "CA1827"]
Specific directory files: ["**/Services/**"]
Fixable only Use suggestedFixableIds from response
